text: 🇲🇽✊ "Honesty is our greatest defense. The best defense of our sovereignty comes from there." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Apatzingán, Michoacán She laid out the three principles of the Fourth Transformation. "For the good of all, first the poor" is humanist thinking and an economic model: what the people pay in taxes returns to them as public works and well-being programs. "There can be no rich government with a poor people," Juárez's principle, is where moral authority comes from. And "with the people everything, without the people nothing": on the judicial reform, she asked whether it is better for judges to be chosen by a few or by the people of Mexico.

🇲🇽⚖️ "No foreign power, no elite decides over the people of Mexico. The people of Mexico hold their destiny in their own hands." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Apatzingán, Michoacán Speaking in Apatzingán days after the 212th anniversary of the 1814 Constitution of Apatzingán, she said that elsewhere in Latin America independence was led by criollo officers, sons of Spaniards with privileges, against the peninsular Spaniards. "Here in Mexico, no. It was the people who rose up in arms." She recalled Hidalgo's execution and Morelos' Sentimientos de la Nación: moderate opulence and indigence, the same education for the landowner's son as for the peon's, and "sovereignty flows from the people," today Article 39 of the Constitution.

🇲🇽🎨 "Think about just one thing: your scholarship and your education are paid for by someone, the people of Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Colima, Colima "Because the people of Mexico, with their taxes, give so that all the young people of our country can have their scholarship and the best education possible. Education opens every door." She told students she entered high school in 1978 at UNAM's CCH Sur, and asked them to cut back on social media: "Not everything is TikTok." Education Secretary Mario Delgado said 400,000 new high-school places will be created by 2030; in Colima seven high schools are being expanded and a new one is being built in Villa de Álvarez.
banner: "THE PEOPLE OF MEXICO PAY FOR IT"

text: 🇲🇽🎨 "This is no longer a social program. It is a constitutional right that belongs to you." — Julio César León Trujillo, national coordinator of Becas para el Bienestar, Colima On October 23 at the University of Colima, Sheinbaum handed out the first Benito Juárez universal scholarship cards of the new cycle. León said the delivery was set for November, but she asked why wait if they could start now. In Colima, more than 57,500 primary students receive Rita Cetina support for supplies and uniforms, 31,400 secondary students the bimonthly Rita Cetina scholarship, and 24,900 high-school students the Benito Juárez scholarship: 115,695 in all. Nationally the system invests 136 billion pesos. High-school applications usually run 1.4–1.5 million a year; this year there were 1.9 million.

🇲🇽✊ "The minimum wage was 2,800 pesos a month in 2018. Today the minimum wage is over 9,500 pesos a month." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Apatzingán, Michoacán She said that in 2018 the people of Mexico, "who have a great memory," chose the Fourth Transformation. The banks still in government hands became banks of the people; Finabien is "the financial institution of the people of Mexico." Well-being programs arrived: the pension for older adults, support for people with disabilities, Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro, La Escuela es Nuestra, Sembrando Vida. In six years poverty and inequality fell. "The well-being programs are public policy grounded in love." In Apatzingán a new Margarita Maza high school is under construction.

🇲🇽✊ "Never again a 'keep quiet, you look prettier.' That's over. Women look prettier when we speak and when we participate." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Apatzingán, Michoacán She said credits on your word reflect a principle of the Fourth Transformation: "It means we trust the people, it means the people rule, and in this case women rule." "Never again should a young woman be told, 'You can't be this, you can't be that, you have no chance.' Women can be whatever we want." She recalled saying, when she took office as Mexico's first woman president, "I don't arrive alone, we arrive," crediting Elvia Carrillo Puerto and the grandmothers and mothers who fought for women's rights.

🇲🇽✊ "We understand credit as a right, a right that promotes economic justice." — Rocío Mejía Flores, director general of Finabien, Apatzingán, Michoacán On October 24 in Apatzingán, Sheinbaum closed the Finabien credits-for-women cycle of the Plan Michoacán for Peace and Justice. With 551 credits handed out that day, the goal she set of 50,000 in Michoacán was met. Mejía said that in two years more than 110,000 credits "on your word" have been granted nationwide, worth 1.8 billion pesos, and more than 56,500 of them in Michoacán. They carry zero interest and need no collateral or guarantor: a woman who receives 10,000 pesos repays 10,000. Another 5,871 ApoyArte credits went to Indigenous artisan women. "Women are the ones who repay their credits best."

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Brent Hits $116, and Mexico Still Charges Zero Tax on Diesel</u>

Brent crude climbed 3.14% on Friday to $116.72 a barrel, its highest level in almost six months, as the US threatens Iran. Hacienda's response, according to El Economista: diesel keeps its 100% IEPS exemption (7.36 pesos per liter) for another week, October 24 to 30, and the extra diesel support rises from 2.35 to 2.63 pesos per liter. The Magna gasoline subsidy falls by 0.74 pesos, to 3.24 pesos per liter, so drivers now pay 3.46 pesos of IEPS, 51.69% of the full rate. Under the voluntary price agreement, regular gasoline stays below 24 pesos per liter and diesel below 27.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Milei Copies Trump and Lists Two Mexican Cartels as Terrorists</u>

Argentina's Javier Milei has added the Sinaloa Cartel and La Nueva Familia Michoacana to his country's terrorist registry, El Soberano reports. Joint Resolution 5/2026 appeared in Argentina's Official Gazette on October 22. Buenos Aires didn't hide where the idea came from: its stated justification is that "the United States and other countries" had already designated the Sinaloa Cartel. When Washington made the same designation in February 2025, Mexico responded by writing a ban on foreign intervention into its Constitution.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>Mexican Workers Raise Money to Send Solar Power to Cuba's Schools and Clinics</u>

The Grupo Internacionalista, the Mexican section of the League for the Fourth International, is raising money from unions and worker organizations to send solar equipment to Cuba, La Jornada reports. The group calls Washington's policy since early this year a "brutal energy strangulation." The goal is at least a dozen complete off-grid units. Each one has eight 620-watt bifacial panels, a 6.2 kW inverter and lithium batteries, and can supply 6 kilowatts continuously. That is enough to run a primary school or a polyclinic. Cuba's school year opened on September 1 in the middle of the blackouts.
